tools.name: check_site
tools.description: Can I scrape this site, and how? Returns a verdict (open, guarded, hostile, blocked), a hostility score, a recommended approach with steps and risks, bot protections, robots.txt and AI-crawler policy, machine-readable surfaces (sitemap, llms.txt, JSON-LD), and eu_ai_training: the signals the EDPB dr

tools.name: get_playbook
tools.description: What should I build with this site, and how? Give a domain and, optionally, a goal in plain words (for example "price alerts", "sales leads", "new jobs", "change log", "knowledge base"). Returns the best-matching workflow for that site: what it does, its cadence, a trigger, collect, shape, store, ac

tools.name: list_sites
tools.description: List the sites in the dataset, optionally by category or verdict. Use it to find easy targets or to see what is covered.

tools.name: xray_page
tools.description: How do I extract the data from THIS page? Fetches one public page and returns a ranked extraction plan: embedded JSON, JSON-LD, repeated records with CSS selectors and field names, tables, feeds, hidden API calls. Each source has a reliability, proof rows pulled from the real page, and the plan note

tools.name: xray_diagram
tools.description: Draw a page's anatomy as an Excalidraw diagram: its regions, the ranked ways to get its data, proof rows, the best route and what the page is made of. Returns a download link for the .excalidraw file (give it to the user; it opens at excalidraw.com or in Obsidian) and a file_name. With include_scene

tools.name: search_sites
tools.description: Find sites in the dataset by a word: a name, host, category (jobs, shop, news, gov), country or verdict. Use it to discover what is covered before calling check_site.

tools.name: can_fetch
tools.description: Does robots.txt allow fetching this exact URL? Fetches the live robots.txt and applies the longest-match rule for a user agent (default: * plus GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, CCBot, PerplexityBot). Returns allowed or not, the rule that decided it, and any crawl delay. A courtesy check, not a le

tools.name: summary
tools.description: Headline numbers across the dataset: verdict mix, how many sites block AI crawlers (and which), protection vendors, by category and country.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "search_sites" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Find sites in the dataset by a word: a name, host, category (jobs, shop, news, gov), country or verdict. Use it to discover what is covered before calling check…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.
